title: Sender-constrained worker Participant credential — C2 profile (DESIGN.md §14.3, §16.6 item 8; family contract R30)
description: The worker-side sender-constrained credential §16.6 item 8 requires. §16 carries no field list (recorded gap — same derived-not-verbatim honesty as the slice-1 DPC profile): this profile transcribes §14.3's normative sentence — a sensitive credential binds token id, proof key (mTLS or DPoP-style, or a local channel-exporter binding), Participant and binding epoch, endpoint incarnation, recovery epoch, audience, surface, operation family, exact subject or preparation scope, nonce, issue time, and short expiry — with the worker's exact subject being its Episode/attempt/fence and its ByomEpisodeBinding. NOTE: the slice-1 DPC schema cites these sentences as §14.4; in the pinned v0.2 text they are §14.3 (recorded gap). Revocation closes live channels and fences queued uses; every runtime mutation additionally presents BOTH current fences (R30/L21). The worker holds no ambient effect authority; a production governed Participant has no parallel ambient credentials for governed resources (§13.2).

nonce.description: Single-use: the (issuer_ref, nonce) pair is atomic (UNIQUE enforced in code).

method.description: Closed §14.3 list: mTLS or DPoP-style proof key, or a local channel-exporter binding.

sender_constraint.description: Sender-constrained, not merely bearer and audience-bound (§14.3).

manifestation_ref.description: The admitted hosted Manifestation this workload incarnates; scheduling fails rather than silently downgrading its security profile (§11.5).

episode_ref.description: The exact Episode: R30 binds the workload identity to exactly one Episode/Manifestation — the credential's exact subject.

byom_fence_epoch.description: A fence advance (new claim, hold, recovery) invalidates this credential; the stale worker may keep bytes as local diagnostic evidence but cannot mutate (§11.3).

byom_episode_binding_ref.description: The exact ByomEpisodeBinding row (byom-episode-binding.schema.json) carrying the dual fences and allowed_local_commitments this worker runs under.

surface.description: Workers exist on the runtime surface only (R30); delivery and continuation ride the Participant channel, never this credential.

allowed_operations.description: Closed operation family: the R30 runtime rows (family contract §2.0). usage_report is evidence, never a meter (§11.4/L33).

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.
